learningHint: Past continuous = was/were + verb‑ing. Use 'was' with singular subject 'she' (She was standing...). Do not use 'were' with 'she', do not replace the subject with 'His', and do not drop the auxiliary 'was'.

subject: they
learningHint: In simple present use the base verb with plural subjects: say 'they stand' (not 'they stands'). Use 'stands' only for he/she/it.

subject: it
english: It is standing on the table.
wrongAnswers: It are standing on the table.
learningHint: Form present continuous with subject + auxiliary (am/is/are) + verb+ing. Use 'is' with 'it' — 'It is standing on the table.' Common mistakes: 'It are...' (wrong auxiliary), 'You standing...' (missing auxiliary), 'She stooding...' (incorrect verb form; say 'She is standing').

subject: I
learningHint: Use 'will' + base verb for the simple future: I will stand here. For the negative say 'I will not' or 'I won't stand here.' For future continuous use 'will be' + -ing (I will be standing here.). Do not use the past form 'stood' or the object pronoun 'me' as the subject, and do not use 'standing' alone after 'will' (it needs 'be'). You can also contract 'I will' to 'I'll'.

subject: we
english: We will be standing at the bus stop.
wrongAnswers: We will standing at the bus stop.
They will be stand at the bus stop.
Us will be standing at the bus stop.
learningHint: Use 'will be' + verb-ing for future continuous: 'We will be standing at the bus stop.' Common mistakes: don't say 'will standing' or 'will be stand'. You can also contract to 'We'll be standing.'

subject: you
wrongAnswers: You was stood under the tree.
learningHint: In the Simple Past, the irregular verb 'stand' becomes 'stood'. Use 'You stood under the tree.' For negatives and questions use 'did' + base verb: 'You did not stand under the tree.' / 'Did you stand under the tree?'. 'You' uses the same past form as 'I' and 'they'.

subject: he
learningHint: Irregular past: 'lose' becomes 'lost' for all subjects (He lost the match). In simple past do not add 'was' or use the present form 'loses' with time words like 'yesterday'. Also use the correct subject pronoun ('he' or 'she'), not 'her'.

subject: she
learningHint: Past continuous = was/were + verb-ing. For singular third-person 'she' use 'was': She was losing her keys. Common mistakes include wrong auxiliary ('us was'), missing auxiliary ('He losing'), or wrong pronoun-verb agreement ('Her were').

subject: they
learningHint: In the simple present with a plural subject like 'they', use the base verb: 'they lose' (not 'they loses'). 'Lose interest' is a common collocation. Note the past tense is 'lost'.

subject: it
learningHint: Use the present continuous: subject + is/am/are + verb‑ing. With 'it' use 'is' → 'It is losing battery power.' When adding -ing to 'lose' drop the silent 'e' (lose → losing). Avoid errors like wrong tense ('it was lose power'), wrong agreement ('they is losing power') or missing auxiliary ('I losing power'). You can also contract 'It is' to 'It's'.

subject: I
learningHint: Use will + base verb for simple future: 'I will lose my temper.' Do not add -s after 'will' (not 'will loses') and use the correct subject pronoun (use 'I', not 'Me').

subject: we
english: We will be losing the game.
wrongAnswers: us will be losing the game.
They will be lose the game.
learningHint: Use future continuous with 'will be' + verb-ing: 'We will be losing the game.' Also remember to use the subject form 'we' (not 'us') and the -ing form of the verb (not the base form 'lose').

subject: you
learningHint: In the simple past the irregular verb 'lose' becomes 'lost' for all subjects: 'You lost your phone.' Do not add 'was' (incorrect: 'you was lost your phone'). Also check possessives—use 'my' for the speaker ('I lost my phone') and 'your' for the listener ('You lost your phone').

subject: he
learningHint: Use the irregular past tense 'paid' (not 'payed'). Structure: subject (he) + past verb (paid) + object (the bill). Also use correct subject pronouns (he, she, I, we, they) — do not use object or possessive forms like 'me' or 'their' as the subject.

subject: she
learningHint: Past continuous structure: subject + was/were + verb‑ing. Use 'was' with singular third person (he/she/it): 'She was paying the rent.' Common mistakes: wrong auxiliary ('she were') or wrong subject‑verb agreement ('you was', 'his was').

subject: they
english: They pay their taxes on time.
wrongAnswers: we pays their taxes on time.
their pay their taxes on time.
they paying their taxes on time.
learningHint: For simple present with plural subjects like 'they', use the base form of the verb (no -s): 'they pay'. 'We pays' is wrong because 'we' takes the base verb 'pay'. 'Their pay' is incorrect because 'their' is a possessive adjective, not the subject 'they'. 'They paying' is ungrammatical for simple present; use 'they pay' or the present continuous 'they are paying'.

subject: it
learningHint: Use present continuous for an ongoing action: subject + be (is for 'it') + verb-ing. Correct: 'It is paying the supplier.' You can also say 'It's paying the supplier.' Avoid using 'are' or a plural auxiliary with 'it.'

subject: I
english: I will pay the fee tomorrow.
wrongAnswers: I will paying the fee tomorrow.
you will payed the fee tomorrow.
me will pay the fee tomorrow.
learningHint: Use 'will' + base verb: 'I will pay'. Time words like 'tomorrow' can go at the end. Common mistakes: do not use '-ing' after 'will' ('I will paying' is wrong), do not use the incorrect past form or spelling ('payed' is wrong — correct is 'paid'), and use the subject pronoun 'I' (not 'me'). You can also say the contracted form 'I'll pay the fee tomorrow.'.

subject: we
english: We will be paying the contractor next week.
malayalam: ഞങ്ങൾ അടുത്ത ആഴ്ച കരാറുകാരനെ പണം കൊടുക്കിക്കൊണ്ടിരിക്കും.
transliteration: njangal adutha aazhcha kararukarane panam kodukkikonduirikkum.
wrongAnswers: we will paying the contractor next week.
they will be pay the contractor next week.
his will be paying the contractor next week.
learningHint: Use 'will be + verb-ing' for the future continuous: 'We will be paying...' indicates an action that will be in progress next week. Common mistakes: 'we will paying...' misses 'be'; 'they will be pay...' uses the base verb instead of '-ing'; 'his will be paying...' uses the wrong pronoun ('his' is possessive). You can also contract it as 'we'll be paying.'

subject: you
english: You pay the courier every week.
malayalam: നിങ്ങൾ ഓരോ ആഴ്ചയും കറിയറിന് പണം കൊടുക്കുന്നു.
transliteration: ningal oro aazhchayum courierkku panam kodukkunnu.
wrongAnswers: you pays the courier every week.
I pay the courier every week.
yours pay the courier every week.
learningHint: In the Simple Present, use the base verb with subjects I/you/we/they: 'you pay' (not 'you pays'). Add -s for he/she/it: 'he pays'. 'Every week' is a frequency expression usually placed at the end: 'You pay the courier every week.' For negatives and questions use do/does: 'You don't (do not) pay...' and 'Does he pay...?'.

subject: he
english: He met her at the station.
wrongAnswers: Her met him at the station.
They meeted her at the station.
He is meet her at the station yesterday.
learningHint: The verb 'meet' is irregular — use 'met' for the past tense (He met her...). Do not add 'is' for past events, and keep correct pronoun order/object: say 'He met her', not 'Her met him'.

subject: she
english: She was meeting him when I arrived.
wrongAnswers: She meet him when I arrive.
learningHint: Past continuous (was/were + verb-ing) describes an action that was in progress at a past time or when another action occurred. With 'she' use 'was' + 'meeting' → 'She was meeting him when I arrived.' Use 'were' for plural subjects (e.g., 'They were meeting'). Avoid using the base verb form (meet) or incorrect auxiliary forms (e.g., 'I were').

subject: they
english: They meet at the park every Saturday.
wrongAnswers: They meets at the park every Saturday.
Their meet at park every Saturday.
Us meet at the park every Saturday.
learningHint: Use the base verb form 'meet' with plural subjects like 'they' in the simple present. Add -s only for third person singular (he/she/it) — e.g. 'He meets at the park.' The phrase 'every Saturday' shows a habitual action. Common mistakes shown: using 'meets' with 'they', using the possessive 'their' instead of the subject, or using the wrong subject like 'us'.

subject: it
learningHint: Use 'is meeting' (present continuous) with the third-person singular subject 'it' to show an ongoing action — that it currently satisfies the requirements. The wrong answers fail because: 'It meeting…' omits the auxiliary 'is'; 'Its meeting…' uses the possessive 'its' instead of the subject 'it'; and 'It were meeting…' uses the wrong auxiliary/tense (should be 'is' for present continuous).

subject: I
wrongAnswers: I will be meet you tomorrow.
learningHint: Use 'will' + base verb to form the simple future. With subject 'I' say 'I will meet you tomorrow.' Do not add another auxiliary ('be') or change 'meet' to past tense ('met').

subject: we
english: We will be meeting the team next week.
malayalam: അടുത്ത ആഴ്ച ഞങ്ങൾ ടീമിനെ കൂടിക്കാഴ്ച നടത്തിക്കൊണ്ടിരിക്കും.
transliteration: aḍutta āḻca ñaṅṅaḷ ṭīmɪnē kūṭikkāḻca naṭattikkoṇṭirikkum.
wrongAnswers: We will be meet the team next week.
Us will be meeting the team next week.
We were meeting the team next week.
learningHint: Future continuous uses 'will be' + verb-ing (we will be meeting). It describes a planned or ongoing action in the future. Common mistakes: do not use the base verb after 'will be' ('will be meet') or a past form ('were meeting'). If you mean a single future event, you can also say 'We will meet the team next week.'

subject: you
learningHint: In the Simple Present with 'you' use the base verb 'meet' (not 'meets'); adverbs of frequency like 'often' usually come after the verb: 'You meet clients often.'

subject: he
english: He included it in the list.
wrongAnswers: Me included it in the list.
They was including it in the list.
She will included it in the list.
learningHint: For simple past use the past form 'included' with the subject (He included it). Do not use object pronoun 'Me' as a subject (use 'I included...'). Use 'they included' (not 'they was including'), and for future say 'will include' (not 'will included').

subject: she
english: She was including him in the group.
wrongAnswers: His was including him in the group.
You were include him in the group.
They is including him in the group.
learningHint: Use past continuous (was + present participle) for third-person singular: 'She was including...'. 'Including' is the present participle and use the object pronoun 'him'. Avoid subject-verb agreement and verb-form errors like 'His was...', 'You were include...', or 'They is including...'.

subject: they
english: They include taxes in the price.
wrongAnswers: I includes taxes in the price.
Her include taxes in the price.
We were include taxes in the price.
learningHint: In the simple present, use the base verb with plural subjects: 'They include...'. For third-person singular (he/she/it) add -s: 'He includes...'. Also use subject pronouns (use 'she' not 'her'), and don’t mix tenses (e.g., 'We were include' is incorrect).

subject: it
learningHint: Present continuous = subject + am/is/are + verb-ing. With 'it' use 'It is including...'. Watch for common errors: wrong pronoun ('Us is including...'), missing auxiliary ('They including...') or wrong tense ('He will including...').

subject: I
english: I will include the summary in the email.
wrongAnswers: She will include the summary in the emailing.
I will including the summary in the email.
Their will include the summary in the email.
learningHint: Use simple future with 'will' + base verb: 'I will include...'. Do not use the -ing form after 'will' (e.g., 'I will including' is wrong). Use 'email' as the noun, not 'emailing' in this context. Also ensure the subject matches: 'Their' is possessive, not a subject; use 'they will' if meaning 'they'.

subject: we
english: We will be including additional examples tomorrow.
wrongAnswers: He will be include additional examples tomorrow.
Me will be including additional examples tomorrow.
They are be including additional examples tomorrow.
learningHint: Use the future continuous: subject + 'will be' + verb‑ing. For example, 'We will be including…'. Do not add extra auxiliaries (e.g., 'are be') or use the wrong subject form.

subject: you
english: You include your contact information on the form.
malayalam: നിങ്ങൾ ഫോംയിൽ നിങ്ങളുടെ കോൺടാക്ട് വിവരങ്ങൾ ഉൾപ്പെടുത്തുന്നു.
transliteration: niṅṅaḷ phōm-il niṅṅaḷuṭe kontākt vivaraṅṅaḷ uḷpeṭunnu.
wrongAnswers: It include your contact information on the form.
You included your contact information on the form.
His includes your contact information on the form.
learningHint: For 'you' in simple present use the base verb 'include' (no -s). Avoid past tense or wrong subject-verb agreement.

subject: he
learningHint: Use the simple past form 'continued' with the subject 'he' — 'He continued his speech.' Common errors here are wrong pronouns ('her continue...'), wrong subject forms ('me continued...') and incorrect auxiliaries ('they is continued...'). For negatives or questions in the past simple use 'did' + base verb: 'He did not continue his speech.' / 'Did he continue his speech?'.

subject: she
learningHint: In past continuous use 'was' for singular third-person subjects (she/he/it) + verb-ing: 'She was continuing the lesson.' Avoid using base verb forms (e.g., 'continue') or incorrect subject-verb agreement as shown in the wrong answers.

subject: they
learningHint: With the plural subject 'they' in simple present use the base verb form: 'They continue...'. For singular third person (he/she/it) add -s: 'She continues...'. Avoid using object pronouns like 'us' as the subject.

subject: it
learningHint: Form present continuous with: subject + am/is/are + verb-ing. Use 'is' with the singular subject 'it' — e.g. 'It is continuing to rain.' 'Continuing' shows the action is ongoing. Avoid incorrect auxiliaries or pronouns such as 'they is', 'it are', or 'her continuing'.

subject: I
learningHint: In simple future use 'will' + base verb (no -s, no -ing). Correct: 'I will continue the project.' Do not use 'continues' after will (we will continues → we will continue), do not use the -ing form (I will continuing → I will continue), and use the correct subject pronoun (use 'he' or 'she', not the possessive 'his').

subject: we
english: We will be continuing the discussion tomorrow.
wrongAnswers: you will be continue the discussion tomorrow.
they will continuing the discussion tomorrow.
it will be continued the discussion tomorrow.
learningHint: Use future continuous: will be + verb-ing to describe an action that will be in progress at a specific time in the future. Correct: 'We will be continuing the discussion tomorrow.' Common errors include omitting 'be' ('you will be continue...'), omitting '-ing' or 'be' ('they will continuing...'), or using the passive form incorrectly ('it will be continued...').

subject: you
learningHint: In present continuous use: subject + correct form of 'to be' + verb‑ing. For 'you' use 'are' → 'You are continuing the course.' Don't use the possessive 'your' or mismatched pronoun‑verb pairs (e.g., 'her is' or 'i are'). You can also use the contraction: 'You're continuing the course.'

subject: he
english: He set the table before dinner.
malayalam: അവൻ રાત્રി ഭക്ഷണത്തിന് മുമ്പ് മേശ સજ્જમാക്കി.
transliteration: avan raatri bhakshanathin munpu mesha sajjamakki.
wrongAnswers: me set the table before dinner.
his was set the table before dinner.
they setted the table before dinner.
learningHint: The past tense of 'set' is the same as the base form: 'set' (not 'setted'). Use the correct subject and verb order: 'He set the table.' 'Set the table' means to arrange plates and utensils. Common mistakes shown: wrong pronoun ('me set') and incorrect verb form ('setted').

subject: she
english: She was setting the alarm when the phone rang.
wrongAnswers: us was setting the alarm when the phone rang.
she were setting the alarm when the phone rang.
her was set the alarm when the phone rang.
learningHint: Past continuous = was/were + verb‑ing. Use 'was' with singular subjects like 'she' to show an action in progress in the past that was interrupted by another past action (e.g., 'She was setting the alarm' when 'the phone rang').

subject: they
english: They set the chairs in a circle every class.
malayalam: അവർ ഓരോ ക്ലാസിലും കസേരകൾ വൃത്തത്തിൽ ക്രമീകരിക്കുന്നു.
transliteration: avar oro klas-ilum kaserakal vrithathil kramikarikkunnu.
wrongAnswers: me sets the chairs in a circle every class.
they is set the chairs in a circle every class.
their setting the chairs in a circle every class.
learningHint: Simple present is used for routines: Subject + base verb (add -s for he/she/it). Use 'they set' (plural subject + base form). 'Me sets' is wrong because 'me' is an object pronoun; 'they is set' has incorrect auxiliary/agreement; 'their setting...' is a possessive/gerund phrase, not a simple present sentence.

subject: it
english: It is setting the alarm for 7 AM.
wrongAnswers: it are setting the alarm for 7 AM.
its is setting the alarm for 7 AM.
you setting the alarm for 7 AM.
learningHint: For present continuous with the subject 'it', use the correct form of 'to be' — 'is' — followed by the verb + -ing: 'It is setting...'. Do not use 'it are' or 'its' (which is possessive). You can also use the contraction: 'It's setting the alarm for 7 AM.'

subject: I
english: I will set the password tonight.
wrongAnswers: he will set the password tonights.
I will be set the password tonight.
me will set the password tonight.
learningHint: Use 'will' + base verb for the simple future: 'I will set the password tonight.' Note: use 'tonight' (not 'tonights'), do not add 'be' after 'will' with an active verb (so not 'will be set'), and use the subject pronoun 'I' (not 'me').

subject: we
english: We will be setting up the equipment tomorrow.
wrongAnswers: we will be set up the equipment tomorrow.
their will be setting up the equipment tomorrow.
we were be setting up the equipment tomorrow.
learningHint: Use 'will be' + verb-ing for the future continuous: 'We will be setting up…' This shows an action that will be ongoing in the future. Avoid passive or incorrect verb forms like 'will be set up', wrong possessive 'their will', or 'we were be' which mixes tenses.

subject: you
english: You set the record last week.
wrongAnswers: you setted the record last week.
yours set the record last week.
you was set the record last week.
learningHint: Tip: 'set' is an irregular verb whose base and past form are the same. Use 'set' for both present and past (e.g., 'You set the record last week.'). Do not add -ed ("setted" is incorrect).

subject: he
learningHint: Use 'learned' (or British 'learnt') for the past tense. With 'he' use the past form: 'He learned the lesson.' Don't use the base form 'learn' or the incorrect passive 'was learned' here. If you add a time word, place it appropriately: 'I learned the lesson yesterday.'

subject: she
learningHint: Past continuous = was/were + verb+ing. Use 'was' with she (She was learning English) and 'were' with plural subjects (They were learning). Use this tense to show an action that was in progress at a past time.

subject: they
learningHint: In the simple present use the base form of the verb with plural subjects: 'They learn new words.' Do not add -s (not 'they learns'). 'Me' is not a subject, and 'They is learning' is wrong; for continuous use 'They are learning new words.'

subject: it
learningHint: Use present continuous: 'it' (singular) takes 'is' + verb-ing, e.g. 'It is learning quickly.' Avoid past tense ('was') or wrong agreement ('are', 'their').

subject: I
learningHint: Form the simple future with 'will' + base verb: 'I will learn the dance.' You can use the contraction: 'I'll learn the dance.' Avoid using 'will' + gerund ('will learning'), incorrect subject forms ('Me will...'), or a past tense ('learnt') for a future event.

subject: we
english: We will be learning the new software.
wrongAnswers: We will learning the new software.
Our will be learning the new software.
We be learning the new software.
learningHint: Form the continuous future with 'will be' + verb+ing: 'We will be learning...'. Do not omit 'be' ('will learning'), change the subject ('Our will be...') or drop auxiliaries ('We be learning').

subject: you
wrongAnswers: You will learn from your mistakes yesterday.
learningHint: In the simple present with subjects you/we/they, use the base verb form (learn). Do not add -s (You learn, not You learns). This tense expresses habitual actions or general truths.

subject: he
learningHint: Use the simple past form 'changed' to show a completed action. Use the subject pronoun 'he' (not the object 'her'), and remember past-tense verbs do not add -s for third-person subjects (He changed, not He changes).

subject: she
learningHint: Use past continuous: subject + was/were + verb-ing. For 'she' use 'was' → 'She was changing her shirt.' Do not use the base form ('change') or the past participle ('changed') with continuous tenses, and use the correct possessive ('her shirt').

subject: they
learningHint: In the simple present, use the base verb with plural subjects: 'they change'. Add -s/-es only with he/she/it (e.g., 'she changes'). Also watch subject choice and tense: 'Us changes' is incorrect subject/verb form and 'They changed' is past tense.

subject: it
learningHint: Present continuous = subject + form of 'be' (am/is/are) + verb-ing. For 'it' use 'is': 'It is changing color.' You can say the contraction 'It's changing color.' Common mistakes: using 'are' with 'it', using 'is' with plural subjects, or omitting the auxiliary verb.

subject: I
wrongAnswers: I will be change my schedule.
learningHint: Use 'will' + base verb (change) for the simple future with subject 'I': 'I will change my schedule.' Do not use 'Me' as the subject ('Me will...'), or forms like 'will changing' or 'will be change'. If you want the progressive form, say 'I will be changing my schedule.'

subject: we
english: We will be changing the design next week.
wrongAnswers: They will be change the design next week.
We will changing the design next week.
Her will be changing the design next week.
learningHint: Use 'will be' + verb-ing to describe an action that will be in progress at a specific future time. Correct: 'We will be changing the design next week.' Common errors: omit 'be' ('will changing'), use base verb after 'be' ('will be change'), or use wrong pronoun ('her' should be 'she').

subject: you
learningHint: Use the past form 'changed' with the subject 'you' — 'You changed your mind.' 'Your' is possessive (not a subject), 'You was changed your mind' has the wrong auxiliary/word order, and 'I changed your mind' uses a different subject and meaning.

subject: he
learningHint: 'Understand' is irregular; its simple past form is 'understood' for all subjects (I, you, he, she, we, they). Do not add -s in the past. For questions/negatives use 'did': 'Did he understand the problem?' / 'He did not understand the problem.'

subject: she
wrongAnswers: You are understanding the lecture yesterday.
learningHint: Past continuous = 'was/were' + verb-ing. Use 'was' with singular subjects (I/he/she/it) and 'were' with plural (we/they/you). It describes an action that was in progress at a past time. Avoid wrong pronouns ('His was...'), confusing past continuous with simple past ('We understood...' is simple past), and mixing present tense with past time markers ('You are understanding... yesterday').

subject: they
learningHint: In the simple present use the base verb with plural subjects: 'They understand...'. Third-person singular adds -s ('He/She understands...'). For negatives and questions use do/does: 'They don't understand.' 'Does he understand?'. This avoids errors like 'I understands' or 'Their understand'.

subject: it
learningHint: Use the auxiliary 'is' with the singular pronoun 'it' and add '-ing' to the main verb: 'It is understanding...'. Also check subject-verb agreement (not 'It understand', 'They is', or 'Her is'). Note: many verbs like 'understand' are stative and usually use the simple present ('It understands the situation') unless you specifically mean an ongoing process.

subject: I
learningHint: Use 'will' + base verb: 'I will understand'. Do not use 'me' as the subject, do not use the '-ing' form ('understanding'), and do not add '-s' to the verb ('understands'). In Malayalam the future is shown by the suffix '-ക്കും' as in 'manassilakkum'.

subject: we
english: We will be understanding the problem.
wrongAnswers: Us will be understanding the problem.
We were be understanding the problem.
learningHint: Form the future continuous with 'will be' + verb-ing. For this sentence: 'We will be understanding the problem.' Avoid using 'us' as subject, using 'were be', or omitting 'be' (e.g., 'He will understanding...').

subject: you
learningHint: In the simple present with 'you' use the base verb form: 'You understand the rules.' Do not add -s. For third-person singular (he/she/it) add -s: 'He understands the rules.' Use 'do/does' for negatives and questions (You do not understand the rules. Do you understand the rules?).

subject: he
learningHint: This is Simple Past: 'watched' shows a completed action. For 'he' use the past form 'watched' (regular verb + -ed). Don't add 's' to form past, and use the correct pronoun and tense (e.g. not 'Her was...' or 'Me watching...' or 'They watches...').

subject: she
learningHint: Past continuous = subject + was/were + verb-ing. For 'she' use 'was', so 'She was watching TV.' Do not add an extra past ending to the -ing form (not 'watchinged'), and match 'was' with singular subjects.

subject: they
learningHint: In the simple present, use the base verb for I/you/we/they: 'They watch the birds.' Add -s only for he/she/it (e.g., 'She watches the birds.'). 'She watching' needs an auxiliary ('She is watching') and 'You watched' is past tense, not simple present.

subject: it
learningHint: Use 'is' with singular third-person subjects (he/she/it) plus the verb + -ing for present continuous: subject + is + verb-ing. Correct: 'It is watching the screen.' Avoid omitting 'is' or using the wrong auxiliary (e.g., 'They is...', 'Me are...', 'He watching...').

subject: I
learningHint: Use 'will' + base verb for simple future: 'I will watch'. Common mistakes: using the -ing form ('I will watching'), using the past form ('We will watched'), or mismatching subject and auxiliary ('His will'). You can also say the contraction: 'I'll watch the match.'

subject: we
english: We will be watching the sunset.
wrongAnswers: Us will be watching the sunset.
She will be watched the sunset.
learningHint: Use 'will be' + verb-ing to describe an action that will be in progress at a future time. Structure: subject + will + be + verb-ing (We will be watching). Negative: We will not (won't) be watching. Question: Will we be watching...?

subject: you
learning hint: In the Simple Present with 'you', use the base verb form 'watch' (no -s). Add -s only for he/she/it (e.g., 'He watches the show'). Malayalam 'നിങ്ങൾ (ningal)' is the polite or plural form of 'you'.

subject: he
learningHint: Use the Simple Past form 'followed' for completed actions: 'He followed the teacher.' Ensure correct subject use ('he' not 'her') and regular verbs form the past by adding -ed; avoid mixing past progressive ('was following') when you mean a completed action.

subject: she
learningHint: Past continuous = subject + was/were + verb-ing. For singular third-person 'she' use 'was', and use the -ing form of the verb: 'She was following the leader.' Avoid using the base verb or the wrong auxiliary.

subject: they
learningHint: In the simple present with plural subjects (they, we), use the base verb: 'They follow the rules.' Don't add -s (that's for he/she/it), don't use past tense like 'followed' for present sentences, and use the correct subject pronoun (use 'they', not 'us' or the possessive 'their').

subject: it
learningHint: For third-person singular subjects (he/she/it) use 'is' + verb-ing: 'It is following the trail.' Change 'follow' to 'following' by adding -ing; do not add an extra 's' or keep the base form after 'is'.

subject: I
wrongAnswers: I will be follows your advice.
learningHint: For Simple Future use: subject + "will" + base verb. Do not add -s or change the verb after "will". Example: "I will follow your advice."

subject: we
english: We will be following the schedule.
wrongAnswers: His will be following the schedule.
They will be follow the schedule.
learningHint: Future continuous is formed with 'will be' + verb-ing (will be following). Use 'will be following' — not 'will following' or 'will be follow'.

subject: you
learningHint: In the simple present, use the base verb with 'you' (no -s): 'You follow'. Also, 'me' is an object pronoun (not a subject), so the correct sentence is 'You follow me.'

subject: he
wrongAnswers: Me was creating a beautiful painting.
They creates a beautiful painting yesterday.
learningHint: This is the simple past. For regular verbs add -ed (create → created). With third-person subjects (he/she/it) use the past form—there is no extra -s. Also use the correct subject pronoun (He, not Her or Me) and avoid present or progressive forms like 'creates' or 'was creating' when you mean simple past.

subject: she
english: She was creating a detailed model.
wrongAnswers: He were creating a detailed model.
Their is creating a detailed model.
I was create a detailed model.
learningHint: Past continuous = subject + was/were + verb-ing. Use 'was' with singular subjects like 'she': 'She was creating a detailed model.' Common mistakes shown: using 'were' with 'she', using the base verb 'create' instead of 'creating', or using a wrong subject ('Their'). Malayalam note: 'srushtichukondirunnu' corresponds to the past continuous form.

subject: they
english: They create new designs every month.
malayalam: അവർ ഓരോ മാസവും പുതിയ ഡിസൈനുകൾ സൃഷ്ടിക്കുന്നു.
transliteration: avar oro masavum puthiya designukal srushtikkunnu.
wrongAnswers: Their create new designs every month.
They creating new designs every month.
She create new designs every months.
learningHint: In the simple present, use the base verb with plural subjects: 'they create' (not 'they creates'). 'They' is a subject pronoun, not the possessive 'their'. For present continuous say 'They are creating'. For 3rd person singular (he/she/it) add -s: 'She creates new designs every month.'

subject: it
english: It is creating a lot of interest.
wrongAnswers: Its is creating a lot of interest.
It are creating a lot of interest.
You is creating a lot of interest.
learningHint: Present continuous = subject + am/is/are + verb-ing. With 'it' use 'is' → 'It is creating a lot of interest.' 'Its' is possessive (not a subject); 'It are' and 'You is' are wrong because the verb does not agree with the subject.

subject: I
english: I will create a plan tomorrow.
wrongAnswers: Me will create a plan tomorrow.
I will creating a plan tomorrow.
We will created a plan tomorrow.
learningHint: Form the simple future with 'will' + base verb (I will create...). Do not use object pronoun 'Me' as the subject or incorrect verb forms like 'creating' or 'created'. Malayalam 'രൂപീകരിക്കും' corresponds to the future meaning 'will create'.

subject: we
english: We will be creating prototypes next week.
wrongAnswers: Us will be creating prototypes next week.
We will be create prototypes next week.
They will be creating prototypes next weeked.
learningHint: Form the future continuous with: subject + 'will be' + verb-ing. Example: 'We will be creating prototypes next week.' You can use the contraction: 'We'll be creating...'. Common mistakes to avoid: don't use the base verb after 'will be' (wrong: 'We will be create...'), and include a future time expression (e.g., 'next week') to clarify the timing.

subject: you
learningHint: In the simple present with 'you', use the base verb form: 'You create'. Only add -s for third-person singular (he/she/it → 'He creates'). Common mistakes: 'You creates' and 'He create' are incorrect.

subject: he
learningHint: The verb 'speak' is irregular: its simple past form is 'spoke' (not 'speaked'). In simple past use the past form directly: 'He spoke to the teacher.' Also ensure correct subject and pronoun: use 'he' (subject) not 'me', and don't add 'is' before a past verb.

subject: she
english: She was speaking on the phone.
wrongAnswers: Us was speaking on the phone.
learningHint: Past continuous = subject + was/were + verb-ing. Use 'was' with 'she' (She was speaking...), include the auxiliary 'was' before the -ing form, and use the phrase 'on the phone.'

subject: they
learningHint: With plural subject 'they' in simple present, use the base verb form: 'They speak...'. Do not add '-s' (wrong: 'They speaks'). Also write 'every day' as two words to mean 'each day'. The wrong answers show common errors: incorrect verb ending, wrong possessive ('Their'), and incorrect auxiliary verb.

subject: it
learningHint: Use 'is' + verb+ing for present continuous with a third-person singular subject like 'it': 'It is speaking softly.' Place the adverb (softly) after the verb. Wrong forms: missing auxiliary ('It speaking...'), wrong subject ('He is...' changes meaning), or incorrect auxiliary ('It were speaking...').

subject: I
english: I will speak at the meeting.
wrongAnswers: Me will speak at the meeting.
I will speaking at the meeting.
learningHint: In Simple Future use 'will' + base verb (e.g., 'I will speak'). In Malayalam the future is marked on the verb (സംസരിക്കും — samsarikkum), and typical word order is subject + place + verb.

subject: we
english: We will be speaking with the manager.
wrongAnswers: We will speaking with the manager.
They will be speak with the manager.
Us will be speaking with manager.
learningHint: Use the Future Continuous to describe an action that will be in progress at a specific time in the future. Form: subject + will be + verb-ing (e.g., 'We will be speaking with the manager.'). Avoid forms like 'will speaking' or 'will be speak'. You can also use the contraction: 'We'll be speaking with the manager.'

subject: you
learningHint: In the simple present with 'you', use the base form of the verb: 'You speak'. Add -s only for third-person singular (he/she/it → 'speaks'). A quick check: I/you/we/they + verb; he/she/it + verb+s.

subject: he
learningHint: Tip: In the simple past, 'read' is spelled the same as the present but pronounced 'red'. Use it for past actions: 'He read the book.' Also check subject forms: use 'She read...' (not 'Her read...'), and for plural use 'They read...'. If you mean continuous past, use 'was/were reading' (e.g., 'They were reading the book').

subject: she
learningHint: Past continuous = was/were + verb-ing. With 'she' use 'was', so use 'reading' (She was reading the letter.). Don't use the past form 'read' here. Note: the past 'read' is pronounced 'red', but 'reading' is pronounced 'reed-ing'.

subject: they
learningHint: In Simple Present, use the base verb form with plural subjects (I/you/we/they) — do not add -s. Example: "They read books." For third-person singular (he/she/it) add -s: "He reads books."

subject: it
wrongAnswers: She was reading the file now.
learningHint: Present continuous = subject + am/is/are + verb+ing. For 'it' use 'is', so use 'It is reading the file.' Avoid incorrect forms like 'They is...' or using past tense 'was' here.

subject: I
english: I will read the novel tomorrow.
wrongAnswers: We will reads the novel tomorrow.
Me will read the novel tomorrow.
They will reading the novel tomorrow.
learningHint: Use 'will' + base verb for the simple future: 'I will read...'. Do not add 's' to the verb after 'will' (not 'reads'), do not use the object form 'Me' as the subject (use 'I'), and do not use the '-ing' form after 'will' (not 'will reading'). The time word 'tomorrow' often signals the simple future.

subject: we
english: We will be reading the chapter tonight.
malayalam: ഞങ്ങൾ ഇന്ന് രാത്രി അധ്യായം വായിച്ചു കൊണ്ടിരിക്കും.
transliteration: njangal innu raathri adhyayam vaayichu kondirikkum.
wrongAnswers: Us will be read the chapter tonight.
He will be readinged the chapter tonight.
She will reading the chapter tonight.
learningHint: Formation: subject + "will be" + verb-ing. Use the present participle (reading), not the past or base form, and use the subject pronoun (we), not object form (us). Example: "We will be reading the chapter tonight." Common mistakes to avoid: "Us will be read...", "will be readinged...", or omitting "be" as in "She will reading...". You can also use the contraction: "We'll be reading...".

subject: you
wrongAnswers: They is read the instructions carefully.
learningHint: Use the base verb form in the simple present with 'you' — 'You read' (pronounced 'reed'). Add -s only for he/she/it (he reads). Note that 'read' spelled the same is the past tense but pronounced 'red'. Also check pronoun form: 'Yours' is incorrect here and 'I reads' and 'They is read' show wrong subject-verb agreement.

subject: he
english: He allowed me to enter the room.
wrongAnswers: They was allowing me to enter.
She will allowed me to enter.
learningHint: Use the simple past 'allowed'. Structure: Subject + allowed + someone + to + base verb (e.g. 'He allowed me to enter'). Use 'me' as the object, not 'I'.

subject: she
english: She was allowing the children to play outside.
malayalam: അവൾ കുട്ടികളെ പുറത്തു കളിക്കാൻ അനുവദിച്ച് കൊണ്ടിരുന്നു.
transliteration: aval kuttiyale purathu kalikkaan anuvadichu kondirunnu.
wrongAnswers: He were allowing the children to play.
Us was allowing kids to play.
They allowed the children to play.
learningHint: Use 'was' with singular subjects (she/he/it) in past continuous: 'she was allowing'. Follow 'allow' in -ing form with the object and 'to' + base verb: 'She was allowing the children to play.' Common mistakes: using 'were' with 'she' or switching to simple past ('allowed').

subject: they
wrongAnswers: They is allowing visitors on Sundays.
learningHint: In simple present, plural subjects use the base verb: 'They allow...'. Avoid 'is' + '-ing' (that's present continuous) — correct continuous form would be 'They are allowing...'. 'His allow...' uses the wrong pronoun (use 'He allows...' for third person singular), and 'You allow...' is grammatically correct but changes the subject.

subject: it
english: It is allowing new users to sign up now.
malayalam: ഇത് ഇപ്പോൾ പുതിയ ഉപയോക്താക്കളെ രജിസ്റ്റർ ചെയ്യാൻ അനുവദിച്ചുകൊണ്ടിരിക്കുന്നു.
transliteration: ith ippol puthiya upayokthakale register cheyyan anuvadichu kondirikkunnu.
wrongAnswers: It were allowing new users to sign up.
Her is allowing users to sign.
They will be allow new users to sign up.
learningHint: Use 'is allowing' with the third-person singular subject 'it' for present continuous (subject-verb agreement). Do not use 'were' with 'it' or 'her is'. For future tense say 'will allow' (not 'will be allow').

subject: I
english: I will allow you to borrow my book.
malayalam: ഞാൻ നിന്നെ എന്റെ പുസ്തകം കടം എടുക്കാൻ അനുവദിക്കും.
transliteration: njan ninne ente pusthakam kadam edukkan anuvadikkum.
wrongAnswers: Me will allow you to borrow my book.
I will allowing you to borrow my book.
They will allow I to borrow my book.
learningHint: For simple future use 'will' + base verb: 'I will allow...'. After 'allow' use the person + 'to' + base verb: 'allow you to borrow'. So the pattern is: Subject + will + verb; allow + object + to + verb. Avoid wrong subject/form (e.g. 'Me will...', 'I will allowing...', 'They will allow I...').

subject: we
english: We will be allowing late submissions next week.
malayalam: ഞങ്ങൾ അടുത്ത ആഴ്ച വൈകിയ സമർപ്പണങ്ങൾ അനുവദിച്ചുകൊണ്ടിരിക്കും.
transliteration: njangal adutha aazhcha vaikya samarpanangal anuvadichu kondirikkum.
wrongAnswers: We will allowing late submissions next week.
Their will be allowing late submissions next week.
You was allowing late submissions next week.
learningHint: This sentence uses the future continuous (will be + verb‑ing) to describe an action that will be in progress in the future: 'We will be allowing...'. Common errors: don't omit 'be' after 'will' ('We will allowing' is wrong); watch pronouns/spelling ('Their' is incorrect here); use correct auxiliary forms ('You was' is incorrect — use 'You were' for past or 'You will be' for future). For a negative: 'We will not be allowing late submissions next week.'

subject: you
english: You were allowing him to speak during the meeting.
transliteration: ningal yogathinide avane samsarikkaan anuvadichu kondirunnu.
wrongAnswers: I was allowing him to speak during the meeting.
You was allowing him to speak during the meeting.
He were allowing him to speak during meeting.
learningHint: Past continuous (past progressive) = was/were + verb-ing. Use 'were' with 'you' -> 'You were allowing...'. The wrong answers show common errors: 'You was...' and 'He were...' are subject-verb agreement mistakes, while 'I was...' changes the subject and so is a different sentence.

subject: he
english: He added sugar to the tea.
wrongAnswers: Me adds sugar to the tea.
They was adding sugar to the tea.
Her will add sugar to the tea.
learningHint: This sentence is in the simple past. The verb 'add' is regular, so use 'added' for completed actions: 'He added sugar to the tea.' Use 'to' to show the recipient ('to the tea'). In Malayalam, 'അവൻ ... ചേർത്തു' shows the same past action.

subject: she
learningHint: Past continuous = subject + was/were + verb‑ing. For singular 'she' use 'was': 'She was adding sugar.' Common mistakes: don't use possessive 'His', don't use 'are' with 'she', and don't combine 'will' with '-ing'. For negative: 'She wasn't adding sugar.' For question: 'Was she adding sugar?'.

subject: they
english: They add salt to the soup.
wrongAnswers: He add salt to the soup.
It were adding salt to the soup.
I added salt to the soup.
learningHint: In the simple present, use the base verb form with plural subjects: 'They add...'. For third-person singular (he/she/it) add -s: 'He adds salt to the soup.'

subject: it
english: It is adding to the total.
wrongAnswers: They is adding to the total.
Us will be adding to the total.
learningHint: Use present continuous with 'is' for third-person singular: 'It is' + verb‑ing. 'It is adding' is correct; avoid 'they is' and incorrect tense forms.

subject: I
learningHint: Use 'I will' + base verb for the simple future (e.g., 'I will add more examples.'). In Malayalam the structure is 'ഞാൻ' + verb-stem + 'ചേർക്കും' (njaan ... cherkum). Common mistakes: do not use '-ing' after 'will' ('We will adding...'), watch subject-verb agreement ('His adds...'), and don't use past tense when you mean future ('You added...').

subject: we
english: We will be adding new features next month.
malayalam: ഞങ്ങൾ അടുത്ത മാസം പുതിയ സവിശേഷതകൾ ചേർക്കുന്നിരിക്കും.
transliteration: njaangal adutha maasam puthiya savishesathakal cherkunnirikkum.
wrongAnswers: I will be add new features next month.
They was adding new features next month.
Her will add new features next month.
learningHint: Form the future continuous with 'will be' + verb-ing (present participle). It describes an action that will be ongoing at a future time: 'We will be adding new features next month.' Common errors: do not use the base verb after 'will be' (wrong: 'will be add'), do not use past continuous for future events ('was adding'), and ensure correct subject pronouns (not 'Her will'). You can also say the contraction: 'We'll be adding...'.

subject: you
english: You add the final paragraph to the report.
wrongAnswers: He add the final paragraph to the report.
They are added the final paragraph to the report.
Me will add the final paragraph to the report.
learningHint: Use the base verb 'add' with the subject 'you' in the simple present (You add...). For third-person singular (he/she/it) add 's' (He adds...). Also avoid wrong pronouns ('Me' should be 'I') and unnecessary auxiliaries ('They are added' is incorrect here).

subject: he
english: He spent his money on books yesterday.
wrongAnswers: her spent money on books today.
I will spends money on books last week.
learningHint: Tip: 'Spend' is an irregular verb — the simple past form is 'spent'. Use Subject + past verb for simple past (He spent...). Use past time markers like 'yesterday'. Avoid adding -s in past tense and avoid mixing past time words with present/progressive or future forms.

subject: she
english: She was spending the evening with her friends.
malayalam: അവൾ കഴിഞ്ഞ വൈകുന്നേരം തന്റെ സുഹൃത്തുക്കളോടൊപ്പം സമയം ചെലവഴിച്ച് കൊണ്ടിരുന്നു.
transliteration: avaḷ kazhinja vaikunnēraṁ tanṟe suhr̥ttukkaḷoṭoppam samayam chelavazhicchu koṇṭirunnu.
wrongAnswers: us was spending evening with friends.
his spend the evening with her yesterday.
you will be spent the evening with them.
learningHint: Past Continuous (Continuous past) describes an action that was ongoing at a specific time in the past. Structure: subject + was/were + verb-ing. For 'she' use 'was' → 'She was spending...'. Common mistakes include wrong subject-verb agreement ('us was...'), wrong auxiliary or tense ('you will be spent...'), and incorrect verb form ('his spend...'). Make sure to use 'spending' (present participle) with 'was' for 'she'.

subject: they
english: They spend an hour exercising every morning.
malayalam: അവർ ഓരോ രാവിലെയും വ്യായാമത്തിനായി ഒരു മണിക്കൂർ ചെലവഴിക്കുന്നു.
transliteration: avar oro raavileyum vyaayaamathinaayi oru manikkoor chelavazhikkunnu.
wrongAnswers: it spend one hour every morning.
her are spending an hour exercise every morning.
they will spend an hour exercising yesterday.
learningHint: This is a simple present sentence describing a routine. Use subject-verb agreement: plural subject 'they' takes the base verb 'spend' (not 'spends' or incorrect pronouns). Present continuous ('are spending') describes an action happening now, and time expressions must match the tense (e.g., don't use 'will' with 'yesterday').

subject: it
english: It is spending too much time processing the data.
malayalam: അത് ഡാറ്റ പ്രോസസ്സ് ചെയ്യുന്നതിന് വളരെ അധികം സമയം ചെലവഴിക്കുന്നത്.
transliteration: athu daata process cheyyunnathin valare adhikam samayam chelavazhich koṇṭirikkunnu.
wrongAnswers: we is spending too much time processing data.
yours spent too much time now.
me will be spending too much time processing the data.
learningHint: For present continuous with a third-person singular subject (it/he/she), use 'is' + verb-ing: e.g., 'It is spending...'. Also use the structure 'spend (too much) time + -ing' for activities: 'spending time processing the data.' Common errors include wrong subject-verb agreement ('we is...') and incorrect pronouns/auxiliaries ('me will be...').

subject: I
english: I will spend my savings on a trip next year.
malayalam: ഞാൻ അടുത്ത വർഷം ഒരു യാത്രക്കായി എന്റെ സമ്പാദ്യം ചെലവഴിക്കും.
transliteration: ñān aṭutta varṣaṁ oru yātrakkāyi ente sampādyaṁ chelavazhikkum.
wrongAnswers: his will spend his savings next year.
they spends my savings on trip next year.
we will spending our savings on a trip next year.
learningHint: Use 'will' + base verb for simple future with 'I'. Correct: I will spend my savings on a trip next year. Common errors: wrong pronoun ('his will spend' → 'he will spend'), wrong verb form ('they spends' → 'they will spend'), and incorrect use of -ing after will ('will spending' → 'will spend').

subject: we
english: We will be spending next month renovating the house.
malayalam: ഞങ്ങൾ അടുത്ത മാസം വീട്ടിന്റെ നവീകരണത്തിനായി സമയം ചെലവഴിച്ച് കൊണ്ടിരിക്കും.
transliteration: ñāṅṅaḷ aṭutta māsam vīṭinṟe navīkaraṇaṭhināyi samayam chelavazhich koṇṭirikkum.
wrongAnswers: he will be spends the month renovating the house.
you spending the month will renovate the house.
their will be spending the month renovating house.
learningHint: Use Future Continuous: 'will be' + verb-ing. With 'we' say 'We will be spending...' (not 'will be spends'). Also watch pronouns ('their' vs 'they're/they will') and place time phrases like 'next month' before the activity: 'spending next month renovating the house.'

subject: you
english: You spend a lot on coffee every week.
malayalam: നിങ്ങൾ ഓരോ ആഴ്ചയും കാപ്പിക്കായി വളരെ അധികം പണം ചെലവഴിക്കുന്നു.
transliteration: niṅṅaḷ oro āzhchayuṁ kāppikkāyi vaḷare adhikaṁ paṇaṁ chelavazhikkunnu.
wrongAnswers: it spends lot on coffee every week.
we spend a lot on coffee last week.
his spend a lot on coffee every week.
learningHint: Tip: In the simple present use the base verb form with I/you/we/they (no -s): 'you spend'. Add -s only for third-person singular (he/she/it) — e.g., 'He spends a lot on coffee every week.' 'Every week' signals a habitual action. For negatives and questions use do/does: 'You don't spend...' / 'Do you spend...?.'

subject: he
learningHint: This sentence is in the simple past tense: 'open' → 'opened'. In simple past the verb form stays the same for all subjects (I/you/he/she/we/they). For negative or question forms use 'did' + base verb (e.g., 'He did not open the door.' / 'Did he open the door?'). Pronounce 'opened' with a /d/ sound at the end.

subject: she
wrongAnswers: She is opening the box yesterday.
learningHint: Past continuous = subject + was/were + verb-ing. Use 'was' with singular subjects like 'she' (She was opening the box). Use subject pronouns (she, not her) and correct agreement ('they were', not 'they was'); do not use present forms like 'is' for past actions.

subject: they
english: They open the shop at nine.
wrongAnswers: They opens the shop at nine.
We open the shop at nine yesterday.
Their open the shop at nine.
learningHint: Use the base verb form with plural subjects in the simple present. Say 'They open' (not 'They opens') for habitual or scheduled actions like opening the shop at nine.

subject: it
learningHint: Use present continuous: subject + am/is/are + verb+ing. For 'it' use 'is' → 'It is opening now.' Errors: 'It opening now.' misses the auxiliary 'is'; 'It was opening now.' uses past continuous ('was'); 'His is opening now.' uses wrong subject (possessive 'his').

subject: I
wrongAnswers: I will be open the window.
learningHint: Use 'will' + base verb for simple future (e.g., 'I will open the window.'). Use the subject 'I' (not 'me') and the base form 'open' (not 'opens' or 'be open').

subject: we
english: We will be opening the store tomorrow.
wrongAnswers: We will opening the store tomorrow.
Us will be opening the store tomorrow.
learningHint: Form the future continuous with: subject + will + be + verb-ing (e.g., 'We will be opening...') to show an action in progress at a future time. Also use the subject pronoun 'we' (not 'us') and use the '-ing' form after 'be'.

subject: you
english: You open the file every morning.
wrongAnswers: You opens the file every morning.
You are open the file every morning.
Yours open the file every morning.
learningHint: In Simple Present with 'you' (second person) use the base verb 'open' — do not add -s. The phrase 'every morning' shows this is a habitual action.

subject: he
wrongAnswers: they was walked to the store.
learningHint: This is the simple past of a regular verb: add -ed to the base verb (walk → walked). In affirmative sentences with 'he' use the past form directly: 'He walked to the store.' For negatives and questions in the past use 'did' + base verb: 'He did not walk to the store.' / 'Did he walk to the store?'

subject: she
english: She was walking in the park.
wrongAnswers: her was walking in the park.
I were walking in the park.
learningHint: Form the past continuous with was/were + verb+ing. Use 'was' for singular third-person subjects: 'She was walking in the park.' Avoid incorrect forms like 'they walking...', 'her was...', or 'I were...'.

wrongAnswers: His was staying with her friend last month.

learningHint: Past continuous uses was/were + verb-ing. For third-person singular 'she' use 'was' + 'staying' — 'She was staying...'. Common errors: using the base verb 'stay' instead of 'staying' or wrong subject-auxiliary agreement (e.g., 'His was...', 'They were stay...').

subject: they

wrongAnswers: Their stays close to the school.

subject: I

learningHint: Use 'will be' + verb-ing for future continuous: 'We will be staying...'. subject: you

wrongAnswers: It cut the paper every morning.

Their reached the office by eight.

subject: it

wrongAnswers: You was reaching the shore now.
She will reach the shore now.

subject: I

He will reaches home by six.
learningHint: Use 'will' + base verb for simple future: 'I will reach...'. Do NOT add 'be' (I will be reach), do NOT add -s (he will reaches), and use the correct subject (I, not us).

subject: we

They will be reach the city by noon.
Yours will be reaching the city by noon.
learningHint: Use 'will be' + verb-ing for the future continuous: 'We will be reaching...'. Common errors: omitting 'be' ("We will reaching..."), using the base form after 'will be' ("They will be reach..."), or using the wrong subject/pronoun ("Yours will be reaching...").
